title: What Cyber Insurers Actually Verify Now
summary: Your cyber insurance application is an attestation about your environment. What underwriters verify in 2026, and where your real coverage limit actually sits.
caption:
A cyber claim is decided twice. Once when the incident happens, and once a year earlier, when someone signed the application.

Most executives read that questionnaire as procurement paperwork. Underwriters read it as a factual description of your environment, and they increasingly ask for evidence instead of taking it on faith.

Three things worth knowing before the next renewal: why the form behaves like an operating specification, why the firewall questions shrank while the identity questions multiplied, and why the loss a mid-sized Los Angeles business is most likely to suffer often sits under a separate sublimit rather than the headline limit.

Written for executives who sign the attestation but have never reconciled it against what their tenant is actually configured to do.
